Chef Jan

By: John Webb | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
South Africa's first Michelin star chef, Jan Hendrik van der Westhuizen, talks to us about his rise to fame in gastronomy's heartland and his planned homecoming.

Unique Selling Point:
Chef Jan is about to embark on the next phase of an already extraordinary life: a much heralded return to his country of birth. He's due to open a fin-dining restaurant in the heart of the Kalahari as well as an innovative test-kitchen in Cape Town. We get to spend two days with him at his acclaimed restaurant in Nice, France to talk about his vision of the future and past successes.

Summary:
France is the culinary centre of the Universe, Nice is the jewel on the Cote D'Azur around which much of it revolves. That Jan Hendrik, fresh off a millionaire's yacht in nearby Monaco, chose to open a restaurant there was always likely to be calamitous. Except, it wasn't. A flair for taste, design and creativity unleashed on an unsuspecting French palate such delights as rusks, chakalaka and pap. And they loved it. Within three short years of opening he was awarded a Michelin star, the culinary world's Nobel prize or Oscar. He is a creative force of nature, a wonderful cook and immensely proud of his roots. In short, an amazing story of a South African who made good.

Extra Budget Items:
One night's accommodation for two in Nice. One return flight to Nice ex Dublin.

Press Release:


The Michelin Chef
A flourishing international career and the culinary world’s most sought-after accolade - South Africa’s first Michelin-star chef Jan Hendrik van der Westhuizen has been living the dream. His restaurant in France has been awarded the coveted Michelin-star accolade - and retained it for three years running. Now he’s heading back to the country of his birth, to open a fine-dining eatery in the heart of the Kalahari and an innovative test-kitchen in Cape Town. Carte Blanche travelled to Nice for a taste of home on the French Riviera.
Producer: John Webb
Presenter: John Webb


Script:


Jan – Script.

VO: In 1900 France, a book was published to get people motoring and boost tyre sales. It offered advice on petrol stations, tyre repair shops, hotels and places to eat. The Michelin guide is now the last word on where to sample the finest food.

VO: Years later, the guide would come to change the life of this little boy.

ITV: Jan Hendrik [00:23:53] I used to have a little restaurant set up in a forest where I grew up and I had my mother's world paintings hanging on the trees and a Persian carpet which I burned. And you know it was to me that was like my little restaurant.

VO: An imaginary restaurant in the woodlands of Middelburg, Mpumalanga. A world away from the one, two, and three-star establishments celebrated in the pages of the Michelin guide.

ITV: Jan Hendrick [00:23:53] I had a big old French cookbook which I read like a bible and I was a child and I remember clearly. I said to myself that's what I want to do one day.

VO: And so, Jan Hendrik van der Westhuizen embarked on a pilgrimage to France. First to Paris and then, via Monaco, to what locals call Nice, la Belle: Nice, the beautiful.

VO: Decades after burning carpets and paging through vintage cookbooks, Jan Hendrik is shopping.

VO: But, he’s not here as a tourist; this is work - a childhood fantasy now the real thing on the French Riviera. While working as a private chef he had a life changing chat with a former employer and, in 2013, the restaurant known simply as Jan opened its doors.

LINK - In Nice, as in the rest of France, you expect world class restaurants serving great food – it is, after all the gastronomic capital of the world. What you don’t expect to find is a restaurant serving pap, chakalaka and rusks.

VO: Or how about Melktert, Rooibos and Koeksisters. They’re regulars on Jan’s menu too. Something I discovered after some in-depth research.

VO: Here, farm favourites meet French flair and so the hors d’oeuvres feature biltong and the starter is mieliepap, tomato, leek and mustard. The tastes are familiar but, somehow, entirely new. It’s home but with a twist.

ITV: Jan Hendrik “STRAP: Jan Hendrik: Chef & Owner, Jan [00:07:18] if you look at something you need to ask yourself what does that taste like. You should even like want to taste wood. That's how important it should be (CUT) It's like wine. It builds up and the next thing you do is you taste like Oh that's gonna work with that and immediately without even tasting it your memory knows these flavors work together.

VO: One of two fish courses comes with a Rooibos broth, and among the meat dishes is a lamb bobotie. (PAUSE) Actually, home with a twist might just describe Jan Hendrik, too.

ITV: Jan Hendrik [00:14:18]I like to see the face who I cook for. It's almost getting just in one minute. Getting to know the person even if it's just seeing a face. I don't think you can cook for strangers.

VO: It’s an approach out of sync with the image of chefs as short tempered and even abusive. That’s not to say Jan Hendrik isn’t consumed by what he does.

ITV: Jan Hendrik [00:28:12]for me not working is working because it's everything I do and everything I experience somehow ties in with the experience I'm going to offer.

John Question: Is that hard?

ITV: Jan Hendrik [00:29:15] No. No. It's a blessing. I mean it's not easy. (CUT) I live fast. I live non-stop.

Link - Looking out at this magnificent city you’d be forgiven for thinking that Jan’s life is all cocktails and canapes, but the reality is very different: and the main reason for that is running a restaurant, cheffing is… well, incredibly difficult.

ITV: Rutger Eysvogel [11:18:33.20] Its constant holidays, good pay and ...... no its hard work. (CUT) you make a lot of sacrifices especially in the calibre that we work at.

VO: Rutger Eysvogel and Carina Garrett are Jan Hendrik’s trusted lieutenants.

ITV: Rutger Eysvogel STRAP “Head Chef, Jan”[11:18:33:20] we all put in easily twelve to fourteen hours a day and it's all passion driven and you want to excel.

ITV: Carina Garrett STRAP “Sous Chef, Jan” [11:19:14.06] (CUT) It's very difficult and it's challenging mentally physically in every possible way. But it is important thing to take care of yourself in your personal life as well otherwise you can't keep up here you know.

VO: That’s because the stresses of a professional kitchen are unrelenting.

VO: Acclaimed US chef and broadcaster, Anthony Bourdain, had the world at his feet yet he took his own life in June last year. His suicide, though not directly related to the pressures of running a restaurant, was an uncomfortable reminder of the thin line between success and torment.

ITV: Jan Hendrik [00:14:18] There is still a big thing about chefs. (CUT) It's cool to do drugs. It's cool to work long hours. It's cool to not ever see sun to have 50 tattoos you know to come to work with a hangover every day. And that's just not happiness you know.

VO: So, at Jan, the burden is eased by a characteristically unique approach to employee welfare, like early-morning yoga overlooking the Mediterranean.

VO: It might seem a trivial sideshow but in this game it’s about self-preservation.

ITV: Jan Hendrik [00:30:32] I always say that just be gentle to yourself [00:31:07] I mean I've sent myself postcards with just the words. Just be kind to yourself be gentle to yourself (CUT) And it just remind yourself of. That's a message from you to you.

VO: Dessert is bitter-sweet apricot followed by preserved peach and another farmhouse staple, evaporated milk. Japie se gunsteling – Japie’s favourite – is pineapple and coconut wizardry.
(PAUSE)

VO: At its worst, cheffing can take a devastating toll. At its best it’s capable of wondrous things.

LINK: A famous French chef once said that good food is the foundation of genuine happiness. And that is the currency of chefs like Jan. It’s not only about ingredients and recipes, it’s also about nostalgia and memories: happiness.

ITV Carina Garrett [11:19:30.24] you have days that are so incredible that it takes away all the bad days. Just one moment (CUT) and that makes you forget and makes it all worthwhile[11:20:04.09] I mean if you can leave somebody with a memory or feeling something positive. People don't remember a lot of things they remember how you made them feel and that's what it's about.

ITV Rutger Eysvogel [11:20:27.13] nobody cooks as good as your mother or your grandmother. If you can get that note of nostalgia, you've got it right.

VO: And getting it right means more than just cooking well.

Jan Hendrik [00:11:27] I don't give a lot (CUT) I give everything. That's really the the main, the main thing is that we, everybody that works in the restaurant everybody that's part of Jan, we literally give everything. But happiness as you said that is the package. And that's not only the food that's the atmosphere that's the music that plays. That's the candle that's burning. It's it's really everything.

VO: With everything in place, maybe, just maybe, you’ll find your way into the pages of a guide originally designed to sell tyres but one that now places you among the world’s best chefs.

Jan Hendrik [00:45:05] we just we got this call one evening from it was a French gentleman. Uh my French was very bad at this stage and he just said uh Bon Soir uh Felicitas. Congratulations you uh your restaurant is just got one star in the Michelin guide. No way. Don't fool with me about shit like this. This is like ridiculous.

VO: Even more ridiculous when you consider it was awarded just three years after the restaurant took its first booking.

Jan Hendrik [00:45:05] (CUT) I mean it was like we won the World Cup in our little world. (CUT) That was really big. It was cheap vodka whatever was close by afterwards.

VO: And in another blow to his stock of cheap Vodka, the team at Jan have retained their Michelin star every year since.

Link – After a fairly philosophical conversation with Jan, it’s appropriate to answer one of the great philosophical questions of our time: and that is, should one of these ever come anywhere near a pizza?

Jan Hendrik [00:55:16] Pineapple on pizza. That's amazing.

John [00:55:20] You think it does?

Jan Hendrik [00:55:25] John just keep thinking about that Monet and that Van Gogh. You know it's it's two different things. What works for one person might not work for another.

VO: And isn’t that as true of life as it is of food?

Ends.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): South Africa's first Michelin star chef, Jan Hendrik van der Westhuizen, talks to us about his rise to fame in gastronomy's heartland and his planned homecoming.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Chef Jan is about to embark on the next phase of an already extraordinary life: a much heralded return to his country of birth. He's due to open a fin-dining restaurant in the heart of the Kalahari as well as an innovative test-kitchen in Cape Town. We get to spend two days with him at his acclaimed restaurant in Nice, France to talk about his vision of the future and past successes.
metadata.Summary: France is the culinary centre of the Universe, Nice is the jewel on the Cote D'Azur around which much of it revolves. That Jan Hendrik, fresh off a millionaire's yacht in nearby Monaco, chose to open a restaurant there was always likely to be calamitous. Except, it wasn't. A flair for taste, design and creativity unleashed on an unsuspecting French palate such delights as rusks, chakalaka and pap. And they loved it. Within three short years of opening he was awarded a Michelin star, the culinary world's Nobel prize or Oscar. He is a creative force of nature, a wonderful cook and immensely proud of his roots. In short, an amazing story of a South African who made good.
